1439.subject: Physics
1439.text: A metallic solid sphere is placed in a uniform electric field. Which path, the lines of force follow as shown in figure?
1439.sol: When metallic solid sphere is placed in a uniform electric field, the electrons of the sphere will move against the direction of the electric field. Consequently, the left face of the sphere acquires negative charge while the right face attains positive charge. The field lines will terminate at the left face of sphere and restart from its right face. The electric field inside the sphere is zero. On the surface of the sphere, the field lines are normal at every point i.e., directed towards the centre. Therefore, the correct field line is represented by line 4 .

During menstrual cycle, levels of LH and

2080.sol: The secretion of gonadotropins (LH and FSH) increases gradually during the follicular phase and stimulates follicular development as well as secretion of estrogens by the growing follicles. Both LH and FSH attain a peak level in the middle of the cycle (about $14^{\text{th }}$ day). Rapid secretion of LH leading to its maximum level during mid-cycle called LH surge induces rupture of Graafian follicle and thereby the release of ovum (ovulation). Concentration of estrogen in blood is also high around $14^{\text{th }}$ day and reaches its peak.

3986.sol:
Vapour phase refining process involves conversion& of a metal& into a volatile compound and then it is decomposed to obtain pure metal.

Nickel& is purified by Mond& process: Impure nickel& is heated in a stream& of carbon monoxide to form a volatile complex which is further decomposed to obtain pure nickel.

$Ni + 4CO\overset{350K}{→}Ni\left(CO\right)^{4}\overset{470K}{→}Ni ( pure ) + 4CO$

Van Arkel method: Zirconium or titanium is purified by this method. Zirconium is heated in iodine vapours to form a volatile complex at $870K$ which is further decomposed to obtain pure metal.

$Zr + 2{I}_{2}\overset{870K}{→}{ZrI}_{4}\overset{1800K}{→}Zr ( pure ) + 2{I}_{2}$&

4531.text: The hybridizations of carbon in graphite, diamond and ${C}_{60}$ are respectively
4531.sol:
Diamond, graphite and ${C}_{60}$ are known as allotropes of carbon. In diamond, each carbon atom is tetrahedrally bonded to four carbon atoms, forming a $3 - D$ network of strong,& covalently bonded carbon atoms. All carbon atoms are ${sp}^{3}$ hybridized.

While in graphite and ${C}_{60}$, each carbon is bonded to three carbon atoms, forming a network of hexagonal rings& arranged in a plane in graphite and as sphere in ${C}_{60}$. All carbon atoms are ${sp}^{2}$& hybridized and have one free electron.& Numerous such layers& are bonded to each other& via weak Van der Waals& forces in graphite.

4999.text:
Identify correct statements from the following:
i. Beryllium oxide is an amphoteric oxide.
ii. Group II elements dissolve in liquid ammonia to form deep blue-black solutions.
iii. The hydration enthalpy of group II ions decreases from \($\mathrm{Be}^{2+}$\) to \($\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}$\).
4999.sol:
All the given statements are correct and their explanations are as follows:
(i) Berylium oxide is an amphoteric oxide, i.e. it can react with both acids and bases.
(ii) Group II elements dissolve in liquid ammonia to form deep blue solutions. This blue colour of the solution is due to the ammoniated electron which absorbs energy in the visible region of light and thus impart blue colour to solution.
\(M+(x+y) \mathrm{NH}_{3} \longrightarrow\left[M\left(\mathrm{NH}}_{3}\right)_x\right]^{2+}+2\left[e\left(\mathrm{NH}}_{3}\right)_y\right]\)
(iii) The hydration enthalpy of group II ions decreases from $\mathrm{Be}^{2+}$ to \( \mathrm{Ba}^{2+}\), as the size of cation increases down the group.

6110.text: An extreme value of $f(x)=\frac{4}{\sin x}+\frac{1}{1-\sin x}$ in $(0, \pi / 2)$ is
6110.sol:
$\because f(x)=\frac{4}{\sin x}+\frac{1}{1-\sin x}\Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=-\frac{4 \cos x}{\sin ^2 x}+\frac{\cos x}{(1-\sin x)^2}$
For critical points: $f^{\prime}(x)=0\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow-\frac{4 \cos x}{\sin ^2 x}+\frac{\cos x}{(1-\sin x)^2}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow-\cos x\left[\frac{4(1-\sin x)^2+\sin ^2 x}{\sin ^2 x(1-\sin x)^2}\right]=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 4(1-\sin x)^2+\sin ^2 x=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 3 \sin ^3 x-8 \sin x+4=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(3 \sin x-2)(\sin x-2)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 3 \sin x-2=0 \text{ or } \sin x=2(\text{ not possible) } \\ & \Rightarrow \sin x=\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}$
So, the only critical value is $x=\sin ^{-1} \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\therefore$f(x)$ has extremum at $x=\sin ^{-1}$\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) 
So,$ the $extreme value is
 \begin{aligned}$& f$\left(\sin ^{-1} \frac{2}{3}\right)=\frac{4}{\sin \left(\sin ^{-1} \frac{2}{3}\right)}+\frac{1}{1-\sin \left(\sin ^{-1} \frac{2}{3}\right)}$\\ & =4 $\times \frac{3}{2}+3=9\end{aligned}$

6209.text: The volume of a spherical balloon is increasing at the rate of $30cc$ per minute. Find the rate of change of surface area of the balloon, when its radius is $6$ cm.
6209.sol:
$⇒ v = \text{volume of sphere of radius}r$

$⇒ v = \dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dv}{dt} = 30cc / min$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dt} \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}\right) =30$

$⇒ \dfrac{4}{3}\pi \left(3r^{2}\right)\dfrac{dr}{dt} =30$

$⇒ \dfrac{dr}{dt} = \dfrac{30}{4\pir^{2}}\left(1\right)$

$⇒ s = \text{surface area of balloon}$

$⇒ s = 4\pir^{2}$

$\text{⇒rate of change of surface area of the balloon} = \dfrac{ds}{dt}$

$⇒ \dfrac{ds}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(4\pir^{2}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{ds}{dt} =8\$ pir$\dfrac{dr}{dt}$$

$⇒ $\dfrac{ds}{dt} =$8\$pir\dfrac{30}{4\pir^{2}} \left(\text{from eq. 1}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{ds}{dt} = \dfrac{60}{r}$

$⇒ \dfrac{ds}{dt} = \dfrac{60}{6} =10{cm}^{2} / min$

6954.text: The angle between the pair of tangents drawn from $(1,1)$ to the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} + 4x + 4y -1 = 0$& is
6954.sol:
Given equation of circle is $x^{2} + y^{2} + 4x + 4y - 1 = 0$

Centre$\left(- 2, - 2\right)$

$OA = OB = r = \sqrt{4 + 4 + 1} = 3$ Where $r$ is radius of circle.

$OC = \sqrt{9 + 9} = 3\sqrt{2}$ (by distance formula)

$⇒ OC^{2} = OA^{2} + CA^{2}$(Pythagoras theorem)

$⇒ CA^{2} = 9$

Now, $sin\alpha = \dfrac{3}{3\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ cos\alpha = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ sin2\alpha = 2sin\alphacos\alpha = 1$

$⇒ sin2\alpha = sin\dfrac{π}{2}$

$⇒ 2\alpha = \dfrac{π}{2}$

So $\dfrac{π}{2}$ is the required angle between the pair of tangents.

& $\frac{2 z-3}{z+4 i}=\frac{(2 x-3)+2 i y}{x+i(y+4)} \times \frac{x-i(y+4)}{x-i(y+4)}$\\
& $=\frac{\left(2 x²-3 x+2 y²+8 y\right)+i(2 x y-2 x y+3 y-8 x+12)}{x^2+(y+4)^2}$\\
& $=\frac{\left(2 x²-3 x+2 y²+8 y\right)+i(12+3 y-8 x)}{x^2+(y+4)^2}$\\
& $\text{ So, } \arg \left(\frac{2 z-3}{z+4 i}\right)=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{12+3 y-8 x}{2 x²-3 x+2 y²+8 y}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4} \quad $$\text{ (given) }$$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad $$\frac{12+3 y-8 x}{2 x²-3 x+2 y²+8 y}=$$1 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 x²+2 y²+5 x+5 y-12=0
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (1) is correct.$

Thus, $\left[\frac{\alpha}{\beta}+\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\right]_{\max }=\left[\frac{18}{k}-2\right]=\left[\frac{18}{k}\right]-2=-2$
where, $\left[\frac{18}{k}\right]=0$ for $k \lt  -18$

12749.sol:
We have, $\begin{array}{ll}& 1+\cos x \cdot \cos5 x=\sin ^2 x \\

\Rightarrow \quad \text{ and } \cos ^2 x+\cos x \cdot \cos5 x=0 \\

\Rightarrow \quad \text{ and } \cos x(2 \cos 3 x \cos 2 x)=0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad \text{ and } \cos x=0 ; \cos 3 x=0 \text{ or } \cos2 x=0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad \text{ and } x=\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3 \pi}{2} \text{ or }\\
& 3 x=\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3 \pi}{2}, \frac{5 \pi}{2}, \frac{7 \pi}{2}, \frac{9 \pi}{2}, \frac{11 \pi}{2} \text{ or }\\
& 2 x=\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3 \pi}{2}, \frac{5 \pi}{2}, \frac{7 \pi}{2}\\
\Rightarrow \quad & x=\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3 \pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{5 \pi}{6}, \frac{7 \pi}{6}, \frac{11 \pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{3 \pi}{4}, \frac{5 \pi}{4}, \frac{7 \pi}{4}
\end{array}$ Thus, there are 10 solutions in $[0,2 \pi]$

19780.subject: Chemistry
options: In $\mathrm{BF}_3$ bond dicopoles are zero but dipole moment is higher.
$\mathrm{O}_2, \mathrm{H}_2$ shown bond diapole due to polarisation.
Dipole moment of ammonia is due to orbital dipole and resultant dipole in same direction.
19780.sol:
The dipole moment of a molecule is a vector quantity, as it has both magnitude and direction. Thus, option (riUg0) is incorrect.

In $\mathrm{BF}_3$, the molecule has a trigonal planar geometry. The individual $\mathrm{B-F}$ bonds are polar, but the resultant dipole moment is zero due to the symmetry of the molecule. Thus, option (HcGbv) is incorrect.

$\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{H}_2$ are homonuclear diatomic molecules. The electronegativity difference between the atoms is zero, so there is no bond dipole moment. Thus, option (KcrsK) is incorrect.

In ammonia ($\mathrm{NH}_3$), the nitrogen atom has a lone pair of electrons. The dipole moment contribution from the lone pair (orbital dipole) and the resultant dipole moment of the three $\mathrm{N-H}$ bonds are in the same direction, which adds up to give a significant net dipole moment. Thus, option (qbbOO) is the correct statement.

Answer: Dipole moment of ammonia is due to orbital dipole and resultant dipole in same direction.

20770.subject: Chemistry
20770.text: In the photoelectric emission, the energy of the emitted electron is:
options: greater than the energy of the incident photon
proportional to the intensity of the incident photon
same as that of the incident photon
smaller than the energy of the incident photon
20770.sol:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electron is given by:

$K_{\max} = E - \Phi$

where $E$ is the energy of the incident photon and $\Phi$ is the work function of the material.

Since the work function $\Phi$ is always positive for any material, the maximum kinetic energy $K_{\max}$ is strictly less than the energy of the incident photon $E$.

The actual kinetic energy of an emitted electron ranges from $0$ to $K_{\max}$.

Therefore, the energy of the emitted electron is always smaller than the energy of the incident photon.

Answer: smaller than the energy of the incident photon

Since, coefficient of $x^{5} and x^{6}$ are equal.

22106.text: In a triangle ABC the coordinate of the vertex A is $(1,2)$. Equations of the median through B and C are respectively $x+y=5$ and $x=4$. Then the equation of side $\mathrm{A B}$ is
22106.sol:
Let the vertices be $A(1, 2)$, $B(x_1, y_1)$, and $C(x_2, y_2)$.

The median through $B$ is $x+y=5$. Since $B$ lies on this line, $x_1+y_1=5$. The midpoint of $AC$ lies on this line, so $\dfrac{1+x_2}{2} + \dfrac{2+y_2}{2} = 5$, which simplifies to $x_2+y_2=7$.

The median through $C$ is $x=4$. Since $C$ lies on this line, $x_2=4$. Substituting into $x_2+y_2=7$, we get $y_2=3$. Thus, $C$ is $(4, 3)$.

The midpoint of $AB$ lies on the median through $C$ ($x=4$), so $\dfrac{1+x_1}{2} = 4$, which gives $x_1=7$.

Using $x_1+y_1=5$ with $x_1=7$, we get $y_1=-2$. Thus, $B$ is $(7, -2)$.

The equation of side $AB$ passing through $A(1, 2)$ and $B(7, -2)$ is given by $y - 2 = \dfrac{-2 - 2}{7 - 1}(x - 1)$.

$y - 2 = \dfrac{-4}{6}(x - 1) = -\dfrac{2}{3}(x - 1)$.

$3y - 6 = -2x + 2$, which simplifies to $2x + 3y = 8$.

Answer: $2 x+3 y=8$

22107.text: The point on the line $x+y=4$ that lie at a unit distance from the line $4 x+3 y=10$ is
22107.sol:
Let the point on the line $x+y=4$ be $P(h, 4-h)$.

The distance $d$ of point $P(h, 4-h)$ from the line $4x+3y-10=0$ is given by the formula $d = \dfrac{|ax_1 + by_1 + c|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$.

Substituting the coordinates of $P$ and the line equation:

$1 = \dfrac{|4(h) + 3(4-h) - 10|}{\sqrt{4^2 + 3^2}}$

$1 = \dfrac{|4h + 12 - 3h - 10|}{\sqrt{16 + 9}}$

$1 = \dfrac{|h + 2|}{5}$

$|h + 2| = 5$

This gives two cases:

Case 1: $h + 2 = 5 \Rightarrow h = 3$. The point is $(3, 4-3) = (3,1)$.

Case 2: $h + 2 = -5 \Rightarrow h = -7$. The point is $(-7, 4-(-7)) = (-7,11)$.

Comparing with the given options, $(-7,11)$ is present.

Answer: $(-7,11)$

22374.subject: Physics
22374.text: A transformer has 400 turns in its primary winding and 800 turns in its secondary winding. The primary voltage is $20 \mathrm{ V}$ and the load in the secondary is 4 ohm. The current in the primary, assuming it to be an ideal transformer, is
22374.sol:
For an ideal transformer, the ratio of voltages is equal to the ratio of the number of turns:

$\dfrac{V_s}{V_p} = \dfrac{N_s}{N_p}$

Given $N_p = 400$, $N_s = 800$, and $V_p = 20 \text{ V}$, we have:

$\dfrac{V_s}{20} = \dfrac{800}{400} = 2$

$V_s = 20 \times 2 = 40 \text{ V}$

The current in the secondary winding $I_s$ is given by Ohm's law with the load resistance $R_s = 4 \Omega$:

$I_s = \dfrac{V_s}{R_s} = \dfrac{40}{4} = 10 \text{ A}$

For an ideal transformer, the power input equals the power output, so $V_p I_p = V_s I_s$:

$20 \times I_p = 40 \times 10$

$20 \times I_p = 400$

$I_p = \dfrac{400}{20} = 20 \text{ A}$

Answer: 20 A

23193.subject: Physics
23193.text: A car, starting from rest, accelerates at the rate (f) through a distance (S), then continues at constant speed for some time $(\mathrm{t})$ and then decelerates at the rate $\dfrac{f}{2}$ to come to rest. If the total distance is 5 S , then
23193.sol:
Let the car accelerate from rest at rate $f$ for distance $S$. The final velocity $v$ reached is given by $v^2 = 0^2 + 2fS$, so $v = \sqrt{2fS}$. The time taken for this phase is $t_1 = \dfrac{v}{f} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2fS}}{f} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2S}{f}}$.

The car then travels at constant speed $v$ for time $t$. The distance covered in this phase is $S_2 = vt = t\sqrt{2fS}$.

Finally, the car decelerates at rate $\dfrac{f}{2}$ to come to rest. Let the distance covered be $S_3$. Using $v^2 = 2aS_3$, we have $v^2 = 2(\dfrac{f}{2})S_3$, which gives $S_3 = \dfrac{v^2}{f} = \dfrac{2fS}{f} = 2S$.

The total distance is given as $5S$. Thus, $S + S_2 + S_3 = 5S$. Substituting the values, $S + t\sqrt{2fS} + 2S = 5S$.

Simplifying, $t\sqrt{2fS} = 2S$. Squaring both sides, $t^2(2fS) = 4S^2$.

Dividing by $2S$ (assuming $S \neq 0$), we get $t^2 f = 2S$, which implies $S = \dfrac{1}{2} f t^2$.

Answer: $S=\dfrac{1}{2} f t^2$

23213.subject: Physics
23213.text: The displacement $x$ of a particle varies with time $t, x=a e^{-p t}+b e^{q t}$, where $a, b, p$ and $q$ are positive constant. The velocity of the particle will
23213.sol:
The displacement of the particle is given by $x = a e^{-pt} + b e^{qt}$, where $a, b, p, q > 0$.

The velocity $v$ is the time derivative of displacement $x$:

$v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(a e^{-pt} + b e^{qt})$

$v = -ap e^{-pt} + bq e^{qt}$

To determine the behavior of velocity with time, we find the acceleration $a_{acc}$ by differentiating $v$ with respect to $t$:

$a_{acc} = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(-ap e^{-pt} + bq e^{qt})$

$a_{acc} = ap^2 e^{-pt} + bq^2 e^{qt}$

Since $a, b, p, q > 0$, the terms $ap^2 e^{-pt}$ and $bq^2 e^{qt}$ are always positive for all $t \ge 0$. Therefore, $a_{acc} > 0$ for all $t$.

Since the acceleration is positive, the velocity $v$ must be an increasing function of time. As $t$ increases, $e^{qt}$ grows exponentially, causing $v$ to increase without bound.

Answer: go on increasing forever

24008.text: Metal-ligand $\pi$-bond formation in $\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$ and $[\text{MnO}_4]^-$ requires electron-pair donation between metal and ligand orbitals. Which one of the following represents the direction of electron-pair donation?
options:
$\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$: metal orbital → ligand orbital
$[\text{MnO}_4]^-$: ligand orbital → metal orbital

$\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$: metal orbital → ligand orbital
$[\text{MnO}_4]^-$: metal orbital → ligand orbital

$\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$: ligand orbital → metal orbital
$[\text{MnO}_4]^-$: ligand orbital → metal orbital

$\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$: ligand orbital → metal orbital
$[\text{MnO}_4]^-$: metal orbital → ligand orbital
24008.sol:
In $\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$, the oxidation state of Mn is $0$. The CO ligand acts as a $\pi$-acceptor. The $\pi$-bond is formed by the synergic back-donation of an electron pair from a filled d-orbital of the metal to the empty $\pi^{*}$ antibonding orbital of the CO ligand. Thus, the direction of electron-pair donation for the $\pi$-bond is metal orbital → ligand orbital.

In $[\text{MnO}_4]^-$, the oxidation state of Mn is $+7$, which corresponds to a $d^0$ electronic configuration. Since the metal has no d-electrons, it cannot donate electrons for $\pi$-bonding. The oxide ligand (\textO^{2-}$) has filled p-orbitals and acts as a \pi$-donor. The $\pi$-bond is formed by the donation of an electron pair from the filled p-orbital of the ligand to the empty d-orbital of the metal. Thus, the direction of electron-pair donation for the $\pi$-bond is ligand orbital → metal orbital.

Answer: $\text{Mn}_2(\text{CO})_{10}$: metal orbital → ligand orbital
$[\text{MnO}_4]^-$: ligand orbital → metal orbital

25153.subject: Chemistry
25153.text:
List-I contains various physical/chemical processes, and List-II contains combinations of changes in enthalpy ($\Delta H$) and entropy ($\Delta S$). Match each entry in List-I to the appropriate entry in List-II, and choose the correct option.
List-IList-II
(P) Physisorption(1) $\Delta H > 0$ and $\Delta S > 0$
(Q) Diamond $\longrightarrow$ Graphite(2) $\Delta H < 0$ and $\Delta S < 0$
(R) Denaturation of protein(3) $\Delta H < 0$ and $\Delta S = 0$
(S) Propene $\longrightarrow$ Cyclopropane(4) $\Delta H > 0$ and $\Delta S < 0$
(5) $\Delta H < 0$ and $\Delta S > 0$
25153.sol:
(P) Physisorption is an exothermic process because attractive forces are formed between the adsorbate and the adsorbent, so $\Delta H < 0$. The gas molecules are restricted on the solid surface, decreasing randomness, so $\Delta S < 0$. This matches (2).

(Q) Diamond $\longrightarrow$ Graphite is an exothermic process because graphite is the thermodynamically more stable allotrope of carbon at standard conditions ($\Delta H < 0$). Graphite has a layered structure and is less dense, so it has higher entropy than the rigid 3D network of diamond ($\Delta S > 0$). This matches (5).

(R) Denaturation of protein involves the breaking of hydrogen bonds and the unfolding of its specific 3D structure into a more random coil. Breaking these interactions requires energy ($\Delta H > 0$) and the unfolding increases randomness ($\Delta S > 0$). This matches (1).

(S) Propene $\longrightarrow$ Cyclopropane is an endothermic process because cyclopropane has significant ring strain compared to the open-chain propene, making it less stable ($\Delta H > 0$). The formation of a rigid ring restricts the degrees of freedom (such as rotation around single bonds), decreasing entropy ($\Delta S < 0$). This matches (4).

Thus, P $\rightarrow$ 2, Q $\rightarrow$ 5, R $\rightarrow$ 1, S $\rightarrow$ 4.

Answer: P $\rightarrow$ 2; Q $\rightarrow$ 5; R $\rightarrow$ 1; S $\rightarrow$ 4

25566.text:
Let $F(x)$ be an indefinite integral of $\sin ^2 x$.

Statement II $\sin ^2(x+\pi)=\sin ^2 x$ for all real $x$.

Statement I is true, Statement II is true; Statement II is not a correct explanation for Statement I.

Statement I is true, Statement II is false

Statement I is false, Statement II is true
25566.sol:
$\begin{aligned}$& F(x)=$\int \sin ^$2 x d x=$\int \frac{1-\cos 2 x}{2}$d x \\
& \Rightarrow F(x)=$\frac{1}{4}($2 x-\sin 2 x)+c
\end{aligned}

Since, $F(x+\pi) \neq F(x)$.
Hence, Statement I is false.
But Statement II is true as $\sin ^2 x$ is periodic with period $\pi$.

26123.text: When light of a given wavelength is incident on a metallic surface, the minimum potential needed to stop the emitted photoelectrons is $6 . 0V$. This potential drops to $0 . 6V$ if another source with wavelength four times that of the first one and intensity half of the first one is used. What are the wavelength of the first source and the work function of the metal, respectively? [Take$\dfrac{hc}{e} = 1 . 24 \times {10}^{- 6}J{mC}^{- 1}$ .]
26123.sol:
According to the Einstein's equation of photoelectric effect for the first case,

$\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - ϕ = 6eV ⋯ ( i )$

And for the second case,

$\dfrac{hc}{4\lambda} - ϕ = 0 . 6eV$

Therefore,

$\dfrac{3hc}{4\lambda} = 5 . 4eV$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{3hc}{4 \times 5 . 4eV} = \dfrac{3 \times 1 . 24 \times {10}^{- 6}}{4 \times 5 . 4}$

$⇒ \lambda = 1 . 72 \times {10}^{- 7}m$

$⇒$ from equation $\left(i\right)$

$\dfrac{hc}{1 . 72 \times {10}^{- 7}} \times \dfrac{1}{1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}} - ϕ = 6eV$

$\dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 25}}{2 . 75 \times {10}^{- 26}} - ϕ = 6$

$⇒ ϕ = \left(7 . 27 - 6\right) ≅ 1 . 2eV$

26583.subject: Physics
26583.text:
List-I shows four planar structures made of uniform solid rods each of mass $m$ and length $l$. In the List-II the possible moment of inertia of these structures about an axis $OCO'$, which lies in the plane of the structures, are given.
Choose the option that describes the correct match between the entries in List-I to those in List-II.
List-IList-II
(P) (1) $\dfrac{5}{4} m l^2$
(Q) (2) $\dfrac{1}{6} m l^2$
(R) (3) $\dfrac{1}{12} m l^2$
(S) (4) $\dfrac{2}{3} m l^2$
(5) $\dfrac{1}{3} m l^2$
26583.sol:
The moment of inertia of a uniform rod of mass $m$ and length $l$ about an axis passing through one end and making an angle $\theta$ with the rod is given by $I = \dfrac{m l^2}{3} \sin^2\theta$.

For structure (P):
The axis $OO'$ makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with both rods $CA$ and $CB$.
$I_P = I_{CA} + I_{CB} = \dfrac{m l^2}{3} \sin^2(45^\circ) + \dfrac{m l^2}{3} \sin^2(45^\circ) = 2 \times \dfrac{m l^2}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{m l^2}{3}$.
This matches with (5).

For structure (Q):
The axis $OO'$ makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with rods $CA$ and $CB$. Rod $AB$ is parallel to the axis at a distance $d = l \sin(60^\circ) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} l$.
$I_Q = I_{CA} + I_{CB} + I_{AB} = 2 \times \left( \dfrac{m l^2}{3} \sin^2(60^\circ) \right) + m d^2$
$I_Q = 2 \times \dfrac{m l^2}{3} \times \dfrac{3}{4} + m \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} l \right)^2 = \dfrac{m l^2}{2} + \dfrac{3 m l^2}{4} = \dfrac{5 m l^2}{4}$.
This matches with (1).

For structure (R):
The axis $OO'$ is the diagonal of the square, making an angle of $45^\circ$ with all four rods.
$I_R = 4 \times \left( \dfrac{m l^2}{3} \sin^2(45^\circ) \right) = 4 \times \dfrac{m l^2}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{2 m l^2}{3}$.
This matches with (4).

For structure (S):
The axis $OO'$ makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with both rods $CA$ and $CB$.
$I_S = 2 \times \left( \dfrac{m l^2}{3} \sin^2(30^\circ) \right) = 2 \times \dfrac{m l^2}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{m l^2}{6}$.
This matches with (2).

Therefore, the correct matching is P$\rightarrow$ 5, Q$\rightarrow$ 1, R$\rightarrow$ 4, S$\rightarrow$ 2.

Answer: P$\rightarrow$ 5, Q$\rightarrow$ 1, R$\rightarrow$ 4, S$\rightarrow$ 2

options: A is false but R is true.
A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
26861.sol:
Alcohols as nucleophile:The bond between $O - H$ is broken when an alcohol reacts as a nucleophile. Alcohols as electrophiles:The bond between $C - O$ is broken when alcohols react as electrophiles.

Alcohols react with active metals such as sodium, potassium and aluminium to yield corresponding alkoxides and hydrogen.

$2R - OH +2 Na \to 2 RONa + {H}_{2}$

Assertion (A) and Reason (R) is correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation.

30095.text: The reaction representing the Mond process for metal refining is ______
30095.sol:
Mond process for metal refining: In this process, nickel is heated in a stream of carbon monoxide forming a volatile complex, nickel tetracarbonyl:

$Ni + 4CO\overset{330 - 350K}{\to}Ni ( CO{)}_{4}$

The carbonyl is subjected to a higher temperature so that it is decomposed giving the pure metal:

$Ni ( CO{)}_{4}\overset{450 - 470K}{\to}Ni + 4CO$

\end{aligned}$
Let the total pressure be $\mathrm{P}$
The pressure exerted by oxygen (partial pressure) $=\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{O}_2} \times \mathrm{P}_{\text{total }} \Rightarrow \mathrm{P} \times \frac{1}{3}$
Hence, (C) is correct.

34506.subject: Mathematics
34506.text:
If the system of linear equations

$2x + 3y - z = - 2$

$x + y + z = 4$

$x - y + \left|\lambda\right|z = 4\lambda - 4$ where $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$,

has no solution, then
34506.sol:
If we have three equations in three variables,

${a}_{1}x + {b}_{1}y + {c}_{1}z = {d}_{1}{a}_{2}x + {b}_{2}y + {c}_{2}z = {d}_{2}{a}_{3}x + {b}_{3}y + {c}_{3}z = {d}_{3}$

then $∆ = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right|$,${∆}_{1} = \left|\begin{cases}{d}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {d}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {d}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right|$,${∆}_{2} = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {d}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {d}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {d}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right|$,${∆}_{3} = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {d}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {d}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {d}_{3}\end{cases}\right|$.

If the set of equations do not have a solution then $∆ = 0$ and at least one among ${∆}_{1}, {∆}_{2}, {∆}_{3}$ is not equal to zero.

$∆ = \left|\begin{cases}2 & 3 & - 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & - 1 & \left|\lambda\right|\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\lambda\right| = 7 ⇒ \lambda = \pm 7 \ldots \left(1\right)$

Case 1: $\lambda = 7$

The system of equations are

$2x + 3y - z = - 2x + y + z = 4x - y + 7z = 24$

$a\left(2x + 3y - z + 2\right) + b\left(x + y + z - 4\right) = \left(x - y + 7z - 24\right)$

Comparing the coefficients of $x$ and $y$ we get,

$2a + b = 13a + b = - 1 ⇒ a = - 2, b = 5$

For these values of $a$ and $b$, coefficients of $z$ and the constant values are matching. So the set of equations will have infinitely many solutions.

Case 2: $\lambda = - 7$

The system of equations are

$2x + 3y - z = - 2x + y + z = 4x - y - 7z = - 32$

$a\left(2x + 3y - z + 2\right) + b\left(x + y + z - 4\right) = \left(x - y - 7z + 32\right)$

Comparing the coefficients of $x$ and $y$ we get,

$2a + b = 13a + b = - 1 ⇒ a = - 2, b = 5$

For these values of $a$ and $b$, coefficients of $z$ and the constant values are not matching. So the set of equations will have no solutions.

35284.text: The function $f: N \to I$ defined by $f\left(x\right) = x - 5\left[\dfrac{x}{5}\right]$ , where $N$ is the set of natural numbers and $\left[x\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$, is:
35284.sol:
Given, $f( x ) = x - 5[ \dfrac{x}{5} ]$

Hence, $f( x ) = 5( \dfrac{x}{5} - [ \dfrac{x}{5} ] )$

$= 5{ \dfrac{x}{5} }$

Since, $x$ is a natural number.

Hence, $\left\{\dfrac{x}{5}\right\} = 0, \dfrac{1}{5}, \dfrac{2}{5}, \dfrac{3}{5}, \dfrac{4}{5}$

Hence, $f( x ) = 0$, when $x = 5n, n \in N$

$= 1$ when $x = 5n + 1, n \in N$

$= 2$ when $x = 5n + 2, n \in N$

$= 3$ when $x = 5n + 3, n \in N$

$= 4$ when $x = 5n + 4, n \in N$

Hence, $f\left(x\right) is neither one-one nor onto.$

35583.subject: Mathematics
35583.text: If $y = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3\cos x - 4\sin x}{4\cos x + 3\sin x}\right) + 2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{1+\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right)$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ is equal to:
35583.sol:
Let $y = y_1 + y_2$

$y_1 = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3\cos x - 4\sin x}{4\cos x + 3\sin x}\right)$

Dividing the numerator and denominator by $4\cos x$:

$y_1 = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{3}{4} - \tan x}{1 + \dfrac{3}{4}\tan x}\right)$

Using the formula $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{A - B}{1 + AB}\right) = \tan^{-1}A - \tan^{-1}B$:

$y_1 = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) - \tan^{-1}(\tan x) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) - x$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy_1}{dx} = -1$

Now, $y_2 = 2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{1+\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right)$

Substituting $x = \sin \theta$:

$y_2 = 2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sin \theta}{1+\cos \theta}\right)$

$y_2 = 2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2\sin(\theta/2)\cos(\theta/2)}{2\cos^2(\theta/2)}\right)$

$y_2 = 2\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) = 2\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) = \theta = \sin^{-1}x$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy_2}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$

At $x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:

$\dfrac{dy_2}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{3}{4}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4}}} = 2$

Therefore, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dy_1}{dx} + \dfrac{dy_2}{dx} = -1 + 2 = 1$

Answer: $1$

36219.text: Let a common tangent to the curves ${y}^{2} = 4x$ and ${\left(x - 4\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 16$ touch the curves at the points $P$ and $Q$. Then ${\left(PQ\right)}^{2}$ is equal to ________.
36219.sol:
Given,

Common tangent to the curves ${y}^{2} = 4x$ and ${\left(x - 4\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 16$ touch the curves at the points $P$ and $Q$

Let, the equation of tangent be,

$y = mx + \dfrac{a}{m}$, where $a = 1$ is focus and $m$ is slope,

So, equation of tangent to parabola will be, $y = mx + \dfrac{1}{m}$

Also line is tangent to circle,

So, using perpendicular distance formula from centre $\left(4, 0\right)$to tangent which will be radius $r = 4$, we get,

$\left|\dfrac{4m + \dfrac{1}{m}}{{m}^{2} + 1}\right| = 4$

$⇒ 16{m}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{{m}^{2}} + 8 = 16{m}^{2} + 16$

$⇒ {m}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$⇒ m = \pm \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$

Now if $m = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$ then $P = \left(\dfrac{a}{{m}^{2}}, \dfrac{2a}{m}\right) = \left(8, 4\sqrt{2}\right)$

Now equation of tangent will be, $x - 2\sqrt{2}y + 8 = 0$

And $Q$ will be foot of perpendicular from $\left(4, 0\right)$ on tangent$x - 2\sqrt{2}y + 8 = 0$ ,

So, using foot of perpendicular formula we get,

$\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y - 0}{- 2\sqrt{2}} = - \dfrac{4 - 0 + 8}{{1}^{2} + {\left(2\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ \left(x, y\right) = \left(\dfrac{8}{3}, \dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)$

Hence, by distance formula we get,

${\left(PQ\right)}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{16}{3}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left(PQ\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{256 + 32}{9} = 32$

36590.text: Let Ajay will not appear in JEE exam with probability $p = \dfrac{2}{7},$ while both Ajay and Vijay will appear in the exam with probability $q = \dfrac{1}{5}$. Then the probability, that Ajay will appear in the exam and Vijay will not appear is:

$⇒ P\left(V\right) = \dfrac{1}{5} \times \dfrac{7}{5}$

$⇒ P\left(V\right) = \dfrac{7}{25}$

The probability that Ajay will appear and Vijay will not appear in the exam is,

$⇒ P\left(A ∩ {V}^{'}\right) = \dfrac{5}{7} \times \dfrac{18}{25}$

$⇒ P\left(A ∩ {V}^{'}\right) = \dfrac{18}{35}$

37013.subject: Mathematics
37013.text: The sum $1 + \dfrac{1}{2}(1^2 + 2^2) + \dfrac{1}{3}(1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2) + \ldots$ upto 10 terms is equal to :
37013.sol:
The $n$-th term of the given series is:

$T_n = \dfrac{1}{n} (1^2 + 2^2 + \ldots + n^2)$

Using the formula for the sum of squares of the first $n$ natural numbers:

$T_n = \dfrac{1}{n} \left( \dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} \right) = \dfrac{(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} = \dfrac{2n^2 + 3n + 1}{6}$

The sum of the first 10 terms is $S_{10} = \sum_{n=1}^{10} T_n$

$S_{10} = \dfrac{1}{6} \left( 2 \sum_{n=1}^{10} n^2 + 3 \sum_{n=1}^{10} n + \sum_{n=1}^{10} 1 \right)$

Using the standard summation formulas:

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} n^2 = \dfrac{10 \times 11 \times 21}{6} = 385$

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} n = \dfrac{10 \times 11}{2} = 55$

$\sum_{n=1}^{10} 1 = 10$

Substituting these values into the sum expression:

$S_{10} = \dfrac{1}{6} (2 \times 385 + 3 \times 55 + 10)$

$S_{10} = \dfrac{1}{6} (770 + 165 + 10)$

$S_{10} = \dfrac{945}{6} = \dfrac{315}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{315}{2}$

37432.text: In a group of $100$ persons $75$ speak English and $40$ speak Hindi. Each person speaks at least one of the two languages. If the number of persons who speak only English is $\alpha$ and the number of persons who speaks only Hindi is $\beta$, then the eccentricity of the ellipse $25\left({\beta}^{2}{x}^{2} + {\alpha}^{2}{y}^{2}\right) = {\alpha}^{2}{\beta}^{2}$ is
37432.sol:
Given,

In a group of $100$ persons $75$ speak English and $40$ speak Hindi,

And each person speaks at least one of the two languages,

And the number of persons who speak only English is $\alpha$ and the number of persons who speaks only Hindi is $\beta$,

Now from above diagram we can see that,

$\beta = 100 - 75 = 25$

So, $\alpha = 75 - \left(40 - 25\right) = 60$

Hence, number of people who speak English only is $\alpha = 60$ and Hindi is $\beta = 25$,

Now putting the value in given equation of ellipse we get,

$25\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{60}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{25}^{2}}\right] = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{36 \times 4} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{25} = 1$

Now comparing with $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$ we get, $a = 12 \text{ and } b = 5$

Now we know that,

Eccentricity of ellipse is given by $e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}}$

$⇒ e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{25}{36 \times 4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{119}}{12}$

37639.text: The median of 100 observations grouped in classes of equal width is 25 . If the median class interval is 20-30 and the number of observations less than 20 is 45 , then the frequency of median class is
37639.sol:
Median is given as

M=l+$\frac{\frac{N}{2}-F}{f} \times$C

where
$l=$ lower limit of the median - class
$f=$ frequency of the median class
$N=$ total frequency
$F=$ cumulative frequency of the class just before the median class
$C=$ length of median class
Now, given, $M=25, N=100, F=45$, $C=20-30=10, l=20$.
$\therefore$ By using formula, we have

$\begin{aligned}$& 25=20+$\frac{50-45}{f} \times$10 \\
& 25-20=$\frac{50}{f} \Rightarrow$5=$\frac{50}{f} \Rightarrow$f=10
\end{aligned}

38009.text: The shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x + 2}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 2} = \dfrac{z - 5}{2}$ and $\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{0}$ is
38009.sol:
Given,

$\dfrac{x + 2}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 2} = \dfrac{z - 5}{2}$

$\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2} = \dfrac{z + 3}{0}$

Now we know that,

Shortest distance between two skew lines is given by,

$SD = \left|\dfrac{\left(\overset{\to}{{a}_{2}} - \overset{\to}{{a}_{1}}\right)\left(\overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}}\right|}\right|$

Now finding, $\overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{{n}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{n}_{2}} = - 4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

And $\overset{\to}{{a}_{2}} - \overset{\to}{{a}_{1}} = \left(4\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k} - \left(- 2\overset{^}{i} + 0\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right)\right) = 6\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}$

Now putting the value in formula we get,

$SD = \left|\dfrac{\left(6\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}\right)\left(- 4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\sqrt{16 + 16 + 4}}\right|$

$⇒ SD = \left|\dfrac{- 24 + 2 - 32}{6}\right| = \dfrac{54}{6} = 9$

38350.text: The sum of all values of $\theta \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ satisfying $\sin^{2}2\theta + \cos^{4}2\theta = \dfrac{3}{4}$ is
38350.sol:
Given $\sin^{2}2\theta + \cos^{4}2\theta = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Using $\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x = 1,$ we get

$⇒ 1 - \cos^{2}2\theta + \cos^{4}2\theta = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Let $\cos^{2}2\theta = t$

$⇒ {t}^{2} - t + \dfrac{1}{4} = 0$

$⇒ {\left(t - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ t = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \cos^{2}2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 2\cos^{2}2\theta - 1 = 0$

Using $cos2A = 2\cos^{2}A - 1,$ we get

$⇒ cos4\theta = 0$

If $cosx = 0,$ then $x = \left(2n + 1\right)\dfrac{\pi}{2}, n \in Z .$

$⇒ 4\theta = \left(2n + 1\right)\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$⇒ \theta = \left(2n + 1\right)\dfrac{\pi}{8}$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{8}, \dfrac{3\pi}{8} \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Hence, the sum of the values of $\theta$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{8} + \dfrac{3\pi}{8} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} .$

${v}^{′} = \dfrac{v}{\sqrt{2}}$

$v = eu$

$e = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$H = h\left(\dfrac{1 + {e}^{2}}{1 - {e}^{2}}\right)$

The total distance covered$= h\left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}}\right) = 3h$

49056.subject: Mathematics
49056.text:
In the figure

Statement-I: When $\alpha > \beta \geq 0$, the section is hyperbola
Statement-II: When $\beta > 90^\circ$, the section is ellipse
Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I is true, Statement II is false
Statement I is false, Statement II is true
49056.sol:
Let $\alpha$ be the semi-vertical angle of the cone and $\beta$ be the angle between the intersecting plane and the axis of the cone.

The conic sections formed by the intersection of a plane and a double cone are determined by the relationship between $\alpha$ and $\beta$:
1. If $0 \le \beta < \alpha$, the plane intersects both nappes of the cone, forming a hyperbola.
2. If $\beta = \alpha$, the plane is parallel to a generator of the cone, forming a parabola.
3. If $\alpha < \beta < 90^\circ$, the plane intersects only one nappe, forming an ellipse.
4. If $\beta = 90^\circ$, the plane is perpendicular to the axis, forming a circle.

From the above conditions, when $\alpha > \beta \ge 0$, the section is a hyperbola. Hence, Statement-I is true.

The angle $\beta$ is defined as the angle between the plane and the axis, which is taken in the range $0^\circ \le \beta \le 90^\circ$. Statement-II claims that for $\beta > 90^\circ$ the section is an ellipse, which is incorrect. Thus, Statement-II is false.

Therefore, Statement I is true and Statement II is false.

Answer: Statement I is true, Statement II is false

49429.subject: Mathematics
49429.text: If $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cl}x^2-1, & 0 < x < 2 \\ 2 x+3, & 2 \leq x < 3\end{array}\right.$,the quadratic equation whose roots are $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{-}} f(x)$ and $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{+}} f(x)$ is
49429.sol:
$f(x)= \begin{cases}x^2-1, & 0 < x < 2 \\ 2 x+3, & 2 \leq x < 3\end{cases}$
Now, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{-}} x^2-1=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left[(2-h)^2-1\right]=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left[4+h^2-4 h-1\right]=4+0-0-1=3$
and $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{+}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{+}}(2 x+3)=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} 2(2+h)+3=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} 4+2 h+3=4+0+3=7$
Therefore, the quadratic equation whose roots are 3 and 7 is given by $x^2-(3+7) x+(3 \times 7)=0$ which is $x^2-10 x+21=0$

52310.text: A particle of mass $2 / 3kg$ with velocity $v = - 15m / s$ at $t = - 2s$ is acted upon by a force $F = k - \betat^{2}$. Here, $k = 8N$ and $\beta = 2N / s^{2}$. The motion is one-dimensional. Then, the speed at which the particle acceleration is zero again, is
52310.sol:
Force on the object is $F = k - \betat^{2}$

Acceleration of the particle,

$a = \dfrac{F}{m} = \dfrac{k - \betat^{2}}{m}$

Acceleration is zero when $k = \betat^{2}$ or $t^{2} = \dfrac{k}{β}$ or $t^{2} = \dfrac{8}{2} ⇒ t = 2s$

Now, $a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{k - \betat^{2}}{m} ⇒ dv = \dfrac{k - \betat^{2}}{m} \cdot dt$

Integrating between given limits, we have 

$⇒ {∫}_{v = - 15}^{v\left(t = 2s\right)}dv = {∫}_{t = - 2s}^{t = 2s}\dfrac{k - \betat^{2}}{m}dt$

$= \dfrac{3}{2}{∫}_{t = - 2}^{t = 2}\left(8 - 2t^{2}\right)dt$

$v\left(t = 2s\right) - \left(- 15\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}{8t - \dfrac{2t^{3}}{3}}_{- 2}^{2}$

$⇒ {v}_{att = 2s} = - 15 + \dfrac{3}{2} \times \left8 \left(2 - \left(-2\right)\right) - \dfrac{2}{3}\left(8 - \left(-2\right)^{3}\right)\right]$

$⇒ {v}_{att = 2s} = - 15 + \dfrac{3}{2} \left(32 - \dfrac{32}{3}\right)$

$= - 15 + \dfrac{3}{2} \left(\dfrac{64}{3}\right)$

$= - 15 + 32 = 17\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$

Denaturation of a protein involves the disruption of its secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures due to the breaking of non-covalent interactions such as hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, and disulfide bridges.

The primary structure, which is the sequence of amino acids linked by strong covalent peptide bonds, is not affected by denaturation and remains intact.

Answer: primary

56418.text: What is the EAN of metal ion in $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ ?
56418.sol:
The effective atomic number (EAN) is calculated using the formula:

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{O.S.} + 2 \times \text{C.N.}$

For the complex $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$:
Atomic number of copper ($Z$) = $29$
Oxidation state of copper ($\text{O.S.}$) = $+2$
Coordination number ($\text{C.N.}$) = $4$

Substituting the values:

$\text{EAN} = 29 - 2 + 2 \times 4$

$\text{EAN} = 27 + 8 = 35$

Answer: $35$

Which of the following net cell reaction takes place in a galvanic cell containing copper electrode and standard hydrogen electrode ?
$\mathrm{E}^{{}^{\circ}}\left(\mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2} \mid \mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{s})}\right)=+0 \cdot 34 \mathrm{ V}$
56850.sol:
Net Cell Reaction Determination via Standard Potentials

A cell's net reaction is governed by standard reduction potentials: the higher potential species undergoes reduction (cathode), while the lower is oxidized (anode). Given $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}|\mathrm{Cu}} = +0.34\ \mathrm{V}$ and $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{2\mathrm{H}^+|\mathrm{H}_2} = 0.00\ \mathrm{V}$, copper ions reduce and hydrogen oxidizes.

Cathode reaction: $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}_{(\mathrm{aq})} + 2\mathrm{e}^- \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{s})}$
Anode reaction: $\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{H}^+_{(\mathrm{aq})} + 2\mathrm{e}^-$

Net cell reaction: $\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}_{(\mathrm{aq})} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{H}^+_{(\mathrm{aq})} + \mathrm{Cu}_{(\mathrm{s})}$

This yields $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\mathrm{cell}} = 0.34\ \mathrm{V} - 0.00\ \mathrm{V} = +0.34\ \mathrm{V}$, confirming spontaneity. Among the options, only B matches this reaction.

Final answer: B

57565.subject: Chemistry
57565.text:
Identify reagent B in following reaction.
$\text{R}-\text{X} \xrightarrow{\ \large{\text{B}}\ } \text{Nitroalkane}$
57565.sol:
The reaction of an alkyl halide with silver nitrite ($\text{AgNO}_2$) yields a nitroalkane as the major product.

$\text{AgNO}_2$ is predominantly covalent in nature. The bond between silver and oxygen ($\text{Ag}-\text{O}$) is covalent, which leaves the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom available for nucleophilic attack.

Therefore, the nucleophilic attack on the alkyl halide occurs through the nitrogen atom, resulting in the formation of a nitroalkane ($\text{R}-\text{NO}_2$).

In contrast, potassium nitrite ($\text{KNO}_2$) is an ionic compound and provides nitrite ions ($\text{NO}_2^-$) in which oxygen is the nucleophilic center, leading to the formation of alkyl nitrites ($\text{R}-\text{O}-\text{N}=\text{O}$).

Thus, reagent B is $\text{Ag}-\text{O}-\text{N}=\text{O}$.

Answer: $\text{Ag} - \text{O} - \text{N} = \text{O}$

57605.subject: Chemistry
57605.text: Which of the following compounds has difficulty in breaking of C-X bond?
57605.sol:
The nucleophilic aromatic substitution mechanism requires electron-withdrawing groups to stabilize the intermediate Meisenheimer complex via resonance. o-Nitrochlorobenzene and p-nitrochlorobenzene position their nitro groups optimally for resonance stabilization of the negative charge at the reaction site.

2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene features three nitro groups providing exceptional resonance stabilization, making its C-Cl bond easiest to cleave.

m-Nitrochlorobenzene cannot provide resonance stabilization to the intermediate since the meta-position nitro group operates primarily through inductive effects. This results in the least stabilized intermediate and therefore the most difficult C-Cl bond cleavage.

60247.text: If $\mathrm{f}(x)=\log (1+x)-\frac{2 x}{2+x}$ then $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is increasing in
60247.sol:
The function $f(x) = \log(1+x) - \frac{2x}{2+x}$ is defined for $x > -1$, as both the logarithmic and rational components require this condition.

The derivative is $f'(x) = \frac{1}{1+x} - \frac{4}{(2+x)^2} = \frac{x^2}{(1+x)(2+x)^2}$.

Since $x^2 \ge 0$ and the denominator $(1+x)(2+x)^2 > 0$ for all $x \in (-1, \infty)$, we have $f'(x) \ge 0$ throughout the domain.

The function is therefore increasing on $(-1, \infty)$, corresponding to option A.

60581.subject: Mathematics
60581.text: The area of smaller part between the circle $x^2+y^2=4$ and the line $x=1$ is _______  sq.units.
60581.sol:
The area of the smaller segment bounded by the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 4$ (radius $r = 2$) and the vertical line $x = 1$ can be determined using integration or geometry.

Using integration, the area is given by $A = 2 \int_{1}^{2} \sqrt{4 - x^2} \, dx$. The standard antiderivative yields:

$A = 2 \left[ \frac{x}{2} \sqrt{4 - x^2} + 2 \sin^{-1} \left( \frac{x}{2} \right) \right]_{1}^{2}$

Evaluating from $x = 1$ to $x = 2$ gives:

$A = 2 \left[ \left( 0 + 2 \cdot \frac{\pi}{2} \right) - \left( \frac{1}{2} \sqrt{3} + 2 \cdot \frac{\pi}{6} \right) \right] = 2 \left( \pi - \frac{\pi}{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \right)$

Simplifying results in $A = \frac{4\pi}{3} - \sqrt{3}$.

The sector area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 4 \cdot \frac{2\pi}{3} = \frac{4\pi}{3}$, and the triangle area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 2\sqrt{3} \cdot 1 = \sqrt{3}$. 61266.subject: Mathematics
61266.text: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{a + bx}{c + dy} represents a family of circles centered at the origin if...$
61266.sol:
The equation of a family of circles centered at the origin is given by $x^2 + y^2 = r^2$, where $r$ is an arbitrary constant.

Differentiating this equation with respect to $x$, we get:

$2x + 2y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x}{y}$

The given differential equation is:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{a + bx}{c + dy}$

For this to represent the family of circles centered at the origin, it must be identical to $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x}{y}$.

Comparing the two equations, we get:

$\dfrac{a + bx}{c + dy} = \dfrac{-x}{y}$

This requires $a = 0$ and $c = 0$. The equation then becomes:

$\dfrac{bx}{dy} = -\dfrac{x}{y}$

$\dfrac{b}{d} = -1$

$b = -d \Rightarrow b + d = 0$

Thus, the required conditions are $a = c = 0$ and $b + d = 0$.

Answer: $a = c = 0,\ b + d = 0$

64459.subject: Mathematics
64459.text: The perimeter a square whose two sides have equations $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+2}{3}=\frac{z-3}{4}$ and $\frac{x}{2}=\frac{y-1}{3}=\frac{z+1}{4}$ is
64459.sol:
Identical direction ratios $2$, $3$, $4$ establish the lines as parallel, implying they are opposite sides of the square.

A point on $L_1$ is $P_1(1, -2, 3)$ and on $L_2$ is $P_2(0, 1, -1)$. The connecting vector is $\vec{P_1P_2} = (-1, 3, -4)$.

The side length $s$ is the perpendicular distance between the parallel lines. Using the direction vector $\vec{d} = (2, 3, 4)$, compute the cross product:

$\vec{P_1P_2} \times \vec{d} = \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} \text{ and } \mathbf{j} \text{ and } \mathbf{k} \\ -1 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } -4 \\ 2 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 4 \end{vmatrix} = 24\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j} - 9\mathbf{k} = (24, -4, -9)$

$|\vec{P_1P_2} \times \vec{d}| = \sqrt{24^2 + (-4)^2 + (-9)^2} = \sqrt{673}$

$|\vec{d}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 3^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{29}$

$s = \frac{\sqrt{673}}{\sqrt{29}}$

The perimeter is $4s = 4 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{673}}{\sqrt{29}} = \frac{4 \sqrt{673}}{\sqrt{29}}$, which corresponds to option B.

65581.subject: Physics
65581.text: In the circuit shown below, the ac source has voltage $V = 30 \cos(\omega t)$ volt with $\omega = 2000$ rad/s. What will be the amplitude of the current?
65581.sol:
From the given circuit, the parameters are:
Amplitude of voltage, $V_m = 30$ V
Angular frequency, $\omega = 2000$ rad/s
Total resistance, $R = 6 + 4 = 10\ \Omega$
Inductance, $L = 5 \times 10^{-3}$ H
Capacitance, $C = 50 \times 10^{-6}$ F

The inductive reactance is:
$X_L = \omega L = 2000 \times 5 \times 10^{-3} = 10\ \Omega$

The capacitive reactance is:
$X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{2000 \times 50 \times 10^{-6}} = 10\ \Omega$

The total impedance of the circuit is:
$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$

Substituting the values:
$Z = \sqrt{10^2 + (10 - 10)^2} = 10\ \Omega$

The amplitude of the current is:
$I_m = \dfrac{V_m}{Z} = \dfrac{30}{10} = 3$ A

Answer: $3$ A

65612.subject: Physics
65612.text: A coil has inductance 2 H. The ratio of its reactance when it is connected first to an a.c. source and then to a d.c. source is
65612.sol:
The inductive reactance is defined as $X_L = \omega L$, where $\omega = 2\pi f$ is the angular frequency. For an AC source ($f_\text{AC} \neq 0$), the reactance is finite: $X_L = 2\pi f_\text{AC} L$.

For DC sources, the frequency is zero ($f_\text{DC} = 0$), yielding $X_L = 2\pi \cdot 0 \cdot L = 0$.

The ratio of reactances is therefore:

$\frac{X_{L_\text{AC}}}{X_{L_\text{DC}}} = \frac{2\pi f_\text{AC} L}{0} = \infty$

As this diverges, the answer is $\boxed{C}$.

67413.text: Six molecules of a gas in container have speeds $2 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}, 5 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}, 3 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$, $6 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}, 3 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ and $5 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$. The r.m.s. speed is
67413.sol:
The root-mean-square speed is calculated using $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{v_1^2 + v_2^2 + \cdots + v_n^2}{n}}$.

Given speeds of $2$ m/s, $5$ m/s, $3$ m/s, $6$ m/s, $3$ m/s, and $5$ m/s, the squares are $4$, $25$, $9$, $36$, $9$, and $25$ m²/s².

The sum is $\Sigma v_i^2 = 4 + 25 + 9 + 36 + 9 + 25 = 108$ m²/s², leading to a mean of $\frac{108}{6} = 18$ m²/s².

Thus, $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{18} \approx 4.2426$ m/s.

This corresponds to the option $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

69158.text: Radius of gyration of a thin uniform circular disc about the axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane is $K_c$. Radius of gyration of the same disc about a diamter of the disc is $K_d$. the ratio $K_d : K_c$ is
69158.sol:
Moment of inertia of a uniform circular disc about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane is $I_c = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2$.

Radius of gyration $K_c = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_c}{M}} = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Moment of inertia of the disc about its diameter is $I_d = \dfrac{1}{4}MR^2$.

Radius of gyration $K_d = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_d}{M}} = \dfrac{R}{2}$.

Ratio $\dfrac{K_d}{K_c} = \dfrac{\dfrac{R}{2}}{\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{2}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Thus, $K_d : K_c = 1 : \sqrt{2}$.

Answer: $1 : \sqrt{2}$

69488.text: In a given logic circuit, the output Y when all the three inputs $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}$ are first low and then high will be respectively
69488.sol:
The circuit output $Y$ is given by the Boolean expression $Y = \bar{A} + \overline{B \cdot C}$.

For all inputs low (A=0$, $B=0$, $C=0$):

\bar{A} = 1$ and $\overline{B \cdot C} = 1$, so $Y = 1$.

For all inputs high (A=1$, $B=1$, $C=1$):

\bar{A} = 0$ and $\overline{B \cdot C} = 0$, so $Y = 0$.

The ordered pair for all inputs low then high is (1,0), corresponding to option C.

69910.sol:

A thermodynamic process in which the volume remains constant is called an isochoric process.

Answer: isochoric process

70956.text: Which fatty acids do not contain double bond between carbon atoms?
70956.sol:
Saturated fatty acids are those fatty acids which do not contain any double bond between carbon atoms in their hydrocarbon chain.

Unsaturated fatty acids contain one or more double bonds between carbon atoms.

Oleic acid is a monounsaturated fatty acid with one double bond.

Linoleic acid is a polyunsaturated fatty acid with two double bonds.

Thus, saturated fatty acids do not contain double bonds.

Answer: Saturated fatty acids

71067.subject: Biology
71067.sol:
Secondary succession occurs in areas where natural biotic communities previously existed but were destroyed or removed due to disturbances such as fire, flood, or human activities.

Abandoned farm lands, cut or burned forests, and flooded lands are examples of areas where secondary succession takes place.

Primary succession occurs in newly formed or exposed areas where no living organisms ever existed, such as newly cooled lava, bare rock, or a newly created pond.

Answer: abandoned farm land

71347.text: A man, homozygous dominant for widows peak (WW), marries a woman with straight hairline homozygous recessive (ww). How many of their off springs will inherit straight hair line?
71347.sol:
The genotype of the man is $WW$ (homozygous dominant for widow's peak).

The genotype of the woman is $ww$ (homozygous recessive for straight hairline).

A cross between the parents (WW \times ww$) will produce offspring that all have the genotype $Ww$ (heterozygous).

Since the allele for widow's peak (W$) is dominant over the allele for straight hairline (w$), all offspring will exhibit the widow's peak phenotype.

Therefore, the percentage of offspring inheriting a straight hairline is 0\ \%$.

Answer: $0\ \%$

71560.subject: Biology
71560.text: Which one of the following does NOT favour absorption of water in plants?
options: Low concentration of solutes in soil water.
71560.sol:
Water absorption in plants depends on several environmental factors.

Low concentration of solutes in soil water means the soil solution is hypotonic, which creates a favourable water potential gradient for water to enter the roots.

Increased transpiration rates create a strong transpirational pull, which is the primary driving force for passive water absorption.

Capillary water is the main source of available water for plants in the soil, so its presence favours absorption.

Poorly aerated soil (such as waterlogged soil) lacks sufficient oxygen for root respiration. This inhibits the metabolic activities of root cells, reduces root growth, and decreases the permeability of cell membranes, thereby significantly reducing water absorption.

Therefore, poorly aerated soil does not favour the absorption of water.

Answer: Poorly aerated soil.

72148.text: A light of wavelength $\lambda(\lambda < \lambda_0)$ falls on a metal surface. The momentum of the fastest moving electron is $p$. In order to have the momentum of an electron equal to $2p$, the required wavelength $\lambda'$ of incident light must be
72148.sol:
Using Einstein's photoelectric equation:

$K_{\max} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}$

Since $K_{\max} = \dfrac{p^2}{2m}$, we have:

$\dfrac{p^2}{2m} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}$

For the new wavelength $\lambda'$, the momentum is $2p$. The new maximum kinetic energy is:

$K'_{\max} = \dfrac{(2p)^2}{2m} = 4 \left( \dfrac{p^2}{2m} \right)

Applying the photoelectric equation again:

4 \left( \dfrac{p^2}{2m} \right) = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda'} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}

Substituting the value of \dfrac{p^2}{2m} from the first equation:

4 \left( \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0} \right) = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda'} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}

Dividing both sides by $ hc$:

\dfrac{4}{\lambda} - \dfrac{4}{\lambda_0} = \dfrac{1}{\lambda'} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_0}

\dfrac{1}{\lambda'} = \dfrac{4}{\lambda} - \dfrac{3}{\lambda_0}

\dfrac{1}{\lambda'} = \dfrac{4\lambda_0 - 3\lambda}{\lambda\lambda_0}

$\lambda' = $\dfrac{\lambda\lambda_0}{4\lambda_0 - 3\lambda}

Answer: \dfrac{\lambda\lambda_0}{4\lambda_0 - 3\lambda}$

Under the Tyndall effect, the longer wavelengths are more transmitted while the shorter wavelengths are more diffusely reflected via scattering. The Tyndall effect is seen when light-scattering particulate matter is dispersed in an otherwise light-transmitting medium, when the diameter of an individual particle is the range of roughly between 40 and 900 nm , i.e. somewhat below or near the wavelengths of visible light $(400-750 \mathrm{ nm})$.

${E}_{a} = 8 . 314 \times 5 \times {10}^{3}{Jmol}^{- 1} = 41 . 5kJ{mol}^{- 1}$

81163.subject: Chemistry
81163.text: The formula of tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride is
81163.sol:
The complex name is tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride.

The central metal ion is cobalt(III), which means $\text{Co}$ is in the $+3$ oxidation state.

The ligands inside the coordination sphere are four ammine ($\text{NH}_3$) molecules which are neutral, one aqua ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) molecule which is neutral, and one chlorido ($\text{Cl}^-$) ion which has a $-1$ charge.

The coordination sphere is $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4(\text{H}_2\text{O})\text{Cl}]$.

The charge on the complex ion is calculated as $+3 + 4(0) + 0 + (-1) = +2$.

To balance the $+2$ charge of the complex ion, two chloride ($\text{Cl}^-$) counter ions are required outside the coordination sphere.

Thus, the formula of the complex is $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4(\text{H}_2\text{O})\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$.

Answer: $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_4(\text{H}_2\text{O})\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$

86417.subject: Mathematics
86417.text: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a function defined by $f(x) = x^5 + x^3$ and let $g(x) = f^{-1}(x)$ be the inverse of $f$. If $g''(2) = \dfrac{a}{b}$ where $a$ and $b$ are positive coprime integers, then the value of $a$ is
86417.sol:
Given $f(x) = x^5 + x^3 and g(x) = f^{-1}(x)$.

By the definition of inverse functions, we have $f(g(x)) = x$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(g(x)) g'(x) = 1 \Rightarrow g'(x) = \dfrac{1}{f'(g(x))}$

Differentiating again with respect to $x$ using the chain rule and quotient rule:

$g''(x) = -\dfrac{f''(g(x)) g'(x)}{(f'(g(x)))^2}$

Substituting $g'(x) = \dfrac{1}{f'(g(x))}$ into the equation:

$g''(x) = -\dfrac{f''(g(x))}{(f'(g(x)))^3}$

To find $g''(2)$, we first determine $g(2)$. Since $f(1) = 1^5 + 1^3 = 2$, it follows that $g(2) = 1$.

Now, we find the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ at $x = 1$:

$f'(x) = 5x^4 + 3x^2 \Rightarrow f'(1) = 5(1)^4 + 3(1)^2 = 8$

$f''(x) = 20x^3 + 6x \Rightarrow f''(1) = 20(1)^3 + 6(1) = 26$

Substituting these values into the expression for $g''(2)$:

$g''(2) = -\dfrac{f''(1)}{(f'(1))^3} = -\dfrac{26}{8^3} = -\dfrac{26}{512} = -\dfrac{13}{256}$

Considering the magnitude to match the positive integers condition given in the problem, we have $\left|g''(2)\right| = \dfrac{13}{256}$.

93823.text: The length of a metal wire is ${l}_{1}$ when the tension in it is ${T}_{1}$ and is ${l}_{2}$ when the tension is ${T}_{2}$. The natural length of wire is
93823.sol:
Let the original length be $l$.

In first case,

Using Hooke's law, $x = \dfrac{T}{K}$

Where, $x$ is the displacement.

We have, ${l}_{1} = l + \dfrac{{T}_{1}}{K}$... (i)

Similarly, ${l}_{2} = l + \dfrac{{T}_{2}}{K}$... (ii)

Solving Equations. (i) and (ii), we get

$l = \dfrac{{l}_{1}{T}_{2} - {l}_{2}{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2} - {T}_{1}}$

93998.text: A $Li 7$ target is bombarded with a proton beam current of magnitude ${10}^{- 4}A$ for an hour to produce $Be 7$ of activity $1. 8 \times {10}^{8}$ disintegrations per second. If we assume that one radioactive nucleus of beryllium is produced by bombarding $1000$& protons, then its half-life is close to
93998.sol:
At time $t$, let say there are $N$ atoms of $Be 7$ (radioactive). Then the net rate of formation of $Be 7$ nuclei at this instant is,

$\dfrac{d ⁡ N ⁡}{d ⁡ t} = \dfrac{1 {0}^{- 4}}{1 \text{.} 6 \times 1 {0}^{- 1 9} \times 1 0 0 0} - \lambda N ⁡$

or $\dfrac{d ⁡ N ⁡}{d ⁡ t} = 6 \text{.} 2 5 \times 1 {0}^{1 1} - \lambda N ⁡$

or ${∫}_{o ⁡}^{N ⁡ 0} \dfrac{d ⁡ N ⁡}{6 \text{.} 2 5 \times 1 {0}^{1 1} - \lambda N ⁡} = {∫}_{0}^{3 6 0 0} d ⁡ t$

where ${N}_{0}$ are the number of nuclei at$t = 1hour$ or $3600s$.

∴ $- \dfrac{1}{\lambda} \text\ln \left(\dfrac{6 \text{.} 2 5 \times 1 {0}^{1 1} - \lambda {N ⁡}_{0}}{6 \text{.} 2 5 \times 1 {0}^{1 1}}\right) = 3 6 0 0$

$\lambda{N}_{0}$ = activity of $Be 7$ at$t = 1hour= 1 . 8 \times {10}^{8}$ disintegrations per second

∴ $- \dfrac{1}{\lambda} \text\ln \left(\dfrac{6 \text{.} 2 5 \times 1 {0}^{1 1} - 1 \text{.} 8 \times 1 {0}^{8}}{6 \text{.} 2 5 \times 1 {0}^{1 1}}\right) = 3 6 0 0$

∴ $\lambda = 8 . 0 \times {10}^{- 8}s^{- 1}$

Therefore, half-life ${t}_{1 / 2} = \dfrac{0\text{.}693}{8\text{.}0 \times 1{0}^{- 8}} = 8\text{.}66 \times 1{0}^{6}s$

& & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & $= 100 . 26$ days$

$

94495.subject: Physics
94495.text: Three rods of material $x$ and three rods of material $y$ of identical length and cross sectional area are connected as shown in the figure. If the end $A$ is maintained at ${60}^{∘}\text{C}$ and the junction $E$ at ${10}^{∘} \text{C}$, then the temperature of junction $C$ is [Given the thermal conductivity of $x$ is $0.92W / m. K$ and that of $\text{y}$ is $0.46W / m. K$]
94495.sol:
Treating the given network of rods in terms of thermal resistance Rx and Ry with

${\text{R}}_{\text{x}} = \dfrac{\text{L}}{\text{A} \times \text{0.92}} \text{and} {\text{R}}_{\text{y}} = \dfrac{\text{L}}{\text{A} \times \text{0.46}} \left[\text{as R} = \dfrac{\text{L}}{\text{AK}}\right]$

so that if   Rx = R,  Ry = 2Rx = 2R

Now as in this bridge [(P/Q) = (R/S)], so the bridge is balanced, i.e., the temperature at junctions C and D is equal and the rod CD becomes ineffective as no heat will flow through it.

Now as the thermal resistance of the bridge between junctions B and E is

$\dfrac{1}{{\text{R}}_{\text{BE}}} = \dfrac{1}{\left(\text{R} + \text{R}\right)} + \dfrac{1}{\left(\text{2R} + \text{2R}\right)} \text{,} \text{i.e.,} {\text{R}}_{\text{BE}} = \dfrac{4}{3} \text{R}$

The total resistance of bridge between A and E will be

      Req = RAB + RBE = 2R + (4/3) R = (10/3) R

So the net rate of flow of heat through the bridge will be

$\dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} = \dfrac{\text{\Delta} \text{\theta}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{eq}}} = \dfrac{\left(\text{60} - \text{10}\right)}{\left(\text{10/3}\right) \text{R}} = \dfrac{\text{15}}{\text{R}}$

Now if TB is the temperature at B,

$[ \dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} {]}_{\text{AB}} = \dfrac{\text{\Delta} \text{\theta}}{{\text{R}}_{\text{AB}}} = \dfrac{\text{60} - {\text{T}}_{\text{B}}}{2 \text{R}}$

$\text{But} [ \dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} {]}_{\text{AB}} = \dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} \text{,} \text{i.e.,} \dfrac{\text{60} - {\text{T}}_{\text{B}}}{2 \text{R}} = \dfrac{\text{15}}{\text{R}} \text{,} \text{i.e.,} {\text{T}}_{\text{B}} = {\text{30}}^{\text{o}} \text{C}$

Also at B

$[ \dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} {]}_{\text{AB}} = [ \dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} {]}_{\text{BC}} + [ \dfrac{\text{dQ}}{\text{dt}} {]}_{\text{BD}}$

$\text{i.e.,} \dfrac{\text{15}}{\text{R}} = \dfrac{\text{30} - {\text{T}}_{\text{C}}}{\text{R}} + \dfrac{\text{30} - {\text{T}}_{\text{D}}}{\text{2R}}$

and as     TC = TD = T,    30 = 3 (30 - T),

i.e.,          TC = TD = T = 20o C

96768.subject: Botany
96768.text: If by radiation all the nitrogenase enzymes are inactivated, then which of the following will not occur? (i) Fixation of atmospheric NO_{2} (ii) Conversion from nitrate to nitrite in legumes (iii) Fixation of nitrogen in legumes (iv) Conversion from ammonium to nitrate in soil
96768.sol: The process by which N_{2} is reduced to NH^{4+} is called nitrogen fixation. Nitrogenase enzyme catalyzes this reduction. It is only carried out by prokaryotic microorganisms. Principle N_{2}-fixers include certain free-living cyanobacteria in symbiotic associations with fungi lichens or with ferns, mosses, and liverworts, and by bacteria or other microbes associated symbiotically with roots, especially those of legumes. About 15 percent of the nearly 20,000 species in the Fabaceae (leguminosae) family have been examined for N_{2} fixation, and approximately 90 percent of these have root nodules in which fixation occurs. So without active nitrogenase enzyme, there will be no N_{2} fixation in legumes.

100102.subject: Physics
100102.text:
Consider the following physical quantities:
Refractive index, Relative density, Solid angle, Strain, Poisson's ratio, Angular frequency, Pressure gradient.

How many of the above quantities are dimensionless?
100102.sol:
Let us evaluate the dimensional formula for each given quantity:

1. Refractive index = $\dfrac{\text{Speed of light in vacuum}}{\text{Speed of light in medium}} \Rightarrow$ Dimensionless $[M^0 L^0 T^0]$
2. Relative density = $\dfrac{\text{Density of substance}}{\text{Density of water}} \Rightarrow$ Dimensionless $[M^0 L^0 T^0]$
3. Solid angle = $\dfrac{\text{Area}}{\text{Radius}^2} \Rightarrow$ Dimensionless $[M^0 L^0 T^0]$
4. Strain = $\dfrac{\text{Change in dimension}}{\text{Original dimension}} \Rightarrow$ Dimensionless $[M^0 L^0 T^0]$
5. Poisson's ratio = $\dfrac{\text{Lateral strain}}{\text{Longitudinal strain}} \Rightarrow$ Dimensionless $[M^0 L^0 T^0]$
6. Angular frequency = $\dfrac{\text{Angle}}{\text{Time}} \Rightarrow [M^0 L^0 T^{-1}]$
7. Pressure gradient = $\dfrac{\text{Pressure}}{\text{Distance}} \Rightarrow \dfrac{[M L^{-1} T^{-2}]}{[L]} = [M L^{-2} T^{-2}]$

There are exactly 5 dimensionless quantities in the given list.

Answer: 5

102889.subject: Physics
102889.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For a uniformly charged solid metallic sphere, the electric potential at its centre is equal to the electric potential at its surface.
Reason (R): The electric field inside a charged solid metallic sphere is zero at all points.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
102889.sol:
For a solid metallic sphere in electrostatic equilibrium, any excess charge resides entirely on its outer surface. Consequently, the electric field $E$ inside the conductor is zero at all points.

The relationship between electric field and electric potential is given by $E = -\dfrac{dV}{dr}$.

Since $E = 0$ everywhere inside the sphere, $\dfrac{dV}{dr} = 0$, which implies that the electric potential $V$ is constant throughout the volume of the sphere.

Therefore, the potential at the centre is exactly equal to the potential at the surface. Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and the zero electric field is the exact mathematical reason why the potential remains constant. Thus, (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

103339.subject: Physics
103339.text: A uniform metal wire of resistance $10 \Omega$ is stretched to double its original length. The stretched wire is then cut into two equal halves. These two halves are connected in parallel across a battery of EMF $12 \text{ V}$ and internal resistance $2 \Omega$. The current drawn from the battery is
103339.sol:
Initial resistance of the wire, $R_0 = 10 \Omega$.

When a wire is stretched to $n$ times its original length, its volume remains constant. The new resistance becomes $R_{new} = n^2 R_0$.
Here, $n = 2$, so $R_{new} = (2)^2 \times 10 = 40 \Omega$.

The wire is then cut into two equal halves. The resistance of each half is proportional to its length, so each half has a resistance of $\dfrac{40}{2} = 20 \Omega$.

These two halves are connected in parallel. The equivalent external resistance $R_{ext}$ is:
$R_{ext} = \dfrac{20 \times 20}{20 + 20} = 10 \Omega$.

The total resistance of the circuit includes the internal resistance of the battery ($r = 2 \Omega$):
$R_{total} = R_{ext} + r = 10 + 2 = 12 \Omega$.

The current drawn from the battery is given by Ohm's law:
$I = \dfrac{E}{R_{total}} = \dfrac{12}{12} = 1 \text{ A}$.

Answer: $1 \text{ A}$

104483.subject: Physics
104483.text: A light ray is incident on one face of a prism of refracting angle $60^{\circ}$. The refractive index of the material of the prism is $\sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}}$. If the ray undergoes grazing emergence at the second face, the angle of incidence is:
104483.sol:
At the second face, for grazing emergence, the angle of refraction is $90^{\circ}$.

Thus, the angle of incidence at the second face is the critical angle $c$.
$\sin c = \dfrac{1}{\mu} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{7}}$
$\cos c = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2 c} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{3}{7}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{7}}$

For a prism, $r_1 + r_2 = A$. Here $r_2 = c$ and $A = 60^{\circ}$.
$r_1 = 60^{\circ} - c$

Applying Snell's law at the first face:
$\sin i = \mu \sin r_1 = \mu \sin(60^{\circ} - c)$
$\sin i = \mu (\sin 60^{\circ} \cos c - \cos 60^{\circ} \sin c)$
$\sin i = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}} \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{7}} - \dfrac{1}{2} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{7}} \right)$
$\sin i = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}} \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{7}} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{7}} \right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}} \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{7}} \right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Therefore, $i = 30^{\circ}$.

Answer: $30^{\circ}$

104801.subject: Physics
104801.text:
Given below are two statements

Statement I: In hydrogen atom, the frequency of radiation emitted when an electron jumps from lower energy orbit $\left({E}_{1}\right)$ to higher energy orbit $\left({E}_{2}\right)$, is given as $hf = {E}_{1} - {E}_{2}$

Statement II: The jumping of electron from higher energy orbit $\left({E}_{2}\right)$ to lower energy orbit $\left({E}_{1}\right)$ is associated with frequency of radiation given as $f = \dfrac{\left({E}_{2} - {E}_{1}\right)}{h}$. This condition is Bohr's frequency condition.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is true.
104801.sol:
According to Bohr's model, when electron makes the transition from lower orbit to higher orbit, its energy can be given as

 $∆ E = {E}_{final} - {E}_{initial} = hf$, here, $h$ is Planck's constant.

Then, $f = \dfrac{{E}_{2} - {E}_{1}}{h}$.

Bohr's frequency condition is the law that state that the frequency of the radiation emitted or absorbed during the transition of an atomic system between two stationary states equals the difference in the energies of the states divided by Planck's constant.

Hence, Statement I is incorrect but statement II is true.

105432.subject: Physics
105432.text: A student uses a standard Vernier calliper ($1$ main scale division = $1$ mm, $10$ Vernier scale divisions = $9$ main scale divisions) which is known to have a negative zero error. The actual thickness of a glass slab is exactly $3.20$ cm. When measuring the slab, the main scale reads $3.1$ cm and the $7^{th}$ Vernier division coincides with a main scale division. Which Vernier division coincides with a main scale division when the jaws of the calliper are brought into contact?
105432.sol:
The least count (LC) of the standard Vernier calliper is:

$\text{LC} = 1 \text{ mm} - 0.9 \text{ mm} = 0.1 \text{ mm} = 0.01 \text{ cm}$

The observed reading during the measurement is:

$\text{Observed reading} = \text{MSR} + (\text{VSR} \times \text{LC}) = 3.1 \text{ cm} + (7 \times 0.01 \text{ cm}) = 3.17 \text{ cm}$

The relationship between actual thickness, observed reading, and zero error is:

$\text{Actual reading} = \text{Observed reading} - \text{Zero error}$

$3.20 \text{ cm} = 3.17 \text{ cm} - \text{Zero error}$

$\text{Zero error} = 3.17 \text{ cm} - 3.20 \text{ cm} = -0.03 \text{ cm}$

For a negative zero error, the zero of the Vernier scale is to the left of the main scale zero. The magnitude of the error is given by:

$\text{Zero error} = -(N - n) \times \text{LC}$

where $N$ is the total number of Vernier divisions ($10$) and $n$ is the coinciding division.

$-0.03 \text{ cm} = -(10 - n) \times 0.01 \text{ cm}$

$10 - n = 3 \implies n = 7$

Thus, the $7^{th}$ Vernier division coincides when the jaws are in contact.

Answer: $7^{th}$

105910.subject: Chemistry
105910.text: Which of the following contains the maximum number of electrons?
105910.sol:
Number of moles $= \dfrac{\text{Given mass}}{\text{Molar mass}}$

Total number of electrons $= \text{Number of moles} \times \text{N}_\text{A} \times (\text{Number of electrons per molecule})$

1) $3.6\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$:
Moles $= \dfrac{3.6}{18} = 0.2\text{ mol}$
Electrons per $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ molecule $= 2(1) + 8 = 10$
Total electrons $= 0.2 \times 10 \times \text{N}_\text{A} = 2.0\text{ N}_\text{A}$

2) $4.0\text{ g}$ of $\text{He}$:
Moles $= \dfrac{4.0}{4} = 1.0\text{ mol}$
Electrons per $\text{He}$ atom $= 2$
Total electrons $= 1.0 \times 2 \times \text{N}_\text{A} = 2.0\text{ N}_\text{A}$

3) $4.4\text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$:
Moles $= \dfrac{4.4}{44} = 0.1\text{ mol}$
Electrons per $\text{CO}_2$ molecule $= 6 + 2(8) = 22$
Total electrons $= 0.1 \times 22 \times \text{N}_\text{A} = 2.2\text{ N}_\text{A}$

4) $3.2\text{ g}$ of $\text{CH}_4$:
Moles $= \dfrac{3.2}{16} = 0.2\text{ mol}$
Electrons per $\text{CH}_4$ molecule $= 6 + 4(1) = 10$
Total electrons $= 0.2 \times 10 \times \text{N}_\text{A} = 2.0\text{ N}_\text{A}$

Thus, $4.4\text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ contains the maximum number of electrons.

Answer: $4.4\text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$

107761.subject: Chemistry
107761.text: Which of the following nitrogen-based polyatomic ions exhibits a linear geometry?
107761.sol:
The geometry of polyatomic ions can be determined using VSEPR theory by evaluating the steric number (number of $\sigma$ bonds + number of lone pairs on the central atom).

For $\text{NO}_2^{-}$, the central nitrogen atom forms two $\sigma$ bonds and has one lone pair. The steric number is $2 + 1 = 3$, corresponding to $sp^2$ hybridization. The presence of one lone pair results in a bent (V-shaped) geometry.

For $\text{NO}_3^{-}$, the central nitrogen atom forms three $\sigma$ bonds and has zero lone pairs. The steric number is 3, corresponding to $sp^2$ hybridization and a trigonal planar geometry.

For $\text{NH}_2^{-}$, the central nitrogen atom forms two $\sigma$ bonds with hydrogen atoms and possesses two lone pairs. The steric number is $2 + 2 = 4$, corresponding to $sp^3$ hybridization. The two lone pairs cause the shape to be bent.

For $\text{NO}_2^{+}$, the central nitrogen atom has 5 valence electrons. Subtracting 1 for the positive charge leaves 4 electrons, which are used to form two double bonds (two $\sigma$ bonds) with two oxygen atoms. There are zero lone pairs on the central nitrogen. The steric number is $2 + 0 = 2$, corresponding to $sp$ hybridization. This results in a linear geometry.

Therefore, $\text{NO}_2^{+}$ is the only ion among the choices with a linear geometry.

Answer: $\text{NO}_2^{+}$

108637.subject: Chemistry
108637.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The magnitude of work done by an ideal gas during a reversible isothermal expansion is maximum compared to an irreversible expansion between the same volume limits.
Reason (R): In a reversible expansion, the external pressure is infinitesimally smaller than the internal pressure of the gas at every stage of the process.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct.
Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct.
108637.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct. The magnitude of work done by a system during expansion is given by the area under the $P-V$ curve. For an isothermal expansion between the same volume limits, the reversible path yields the maximum magnitude of work.

Reason (R) is correct and explains the Assertion. Work done is given by $w = -\int P_{\text{ext}} dV$. To maximize the magnitude of expansion work, the opposing external pressure ($P_{\text{ext}}$) must be as large as possible. In a reversible expansion, $P_{\text{ext}}$ is kept infinitesimally smaller than the internal pressure of the gas ($P_{\text{int}}$) at every stage ($P_{\text{ext}} = P_{\text{int}} - dp$). This ensures that the maximum possible external pressure opposes the expansion, leading to the maximum magnitude of work.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

114391.subject: Chemistry
114391.text: A conductivity cell having a cell constant of $1.2 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ is filled with a $0.1 \text{ M}$ electrolyte solution. If the conductivity of this solution is $2.4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ S cm}^{-1}$, what is the resistance of the cell?
114391.sol:
The relationship between cell constant ($G^*$), conductivity ($\kappa$), and resistance ($R$) is given by:

$G^* = \kappa \times R$

Rearranging the formula to solve for resistance:

$R = \dfrac{G^*}{\kappa}$

Substituting the given values:

$R = \dfrac{1.2 \text{ cm}^{-1}}{2.4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ S cm}^{-1}} = 500 \text{ }\Omega$

The concentration of the solution ($0.1 \text{ M}$) is extraneous information for this calculation.

Answer: $500 \text{ }\Omega$

119886.subject: Chemistry
119886.text:
Consider the molecule 4-amino-$N$-(2-aminoethyl)benzamide, which contains three distinct nitrogen atoms labelled as follows:
(a) The nitrogen of the terminal aliphatic primary amine group
(b) The nitrogen of the amide group
(c) The nitrogen of the aromatic primary amine group

What is the correct decreasing order of basic strength of these labelled nitrogen atoms?
119886.sol:
The basicity of a nitrogen atom depends on the availability of its lone pair for protonation.

Nitrogen (a) belongs to an aliphatic primary amine. Its lone pair is localized and its electron density is increased by the +I effect of the alkyl chain, making it the most basic site.

Nitrogen (c) belongs to an aromatic primary amine (aniline derivative). Its lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring via resonance, making it less basic than the aliphatic amine.

Nitrogen (b) belongs to an amide group. Its lone pair is strongly delocalized onto the highly electronegative carbonyl oxygen atom via resonance. This makes the amide nitrogen the least basic of the three.

Therefore, the correct decreasing order of basic strength is (a) > (c) > (b).

Answer: (a) > (c) > (b)

122083.sol:
Spermatophyte, also called seed plant or phanerogam are seed-bearing tracheophytes (vascular plants). They are characterised by reproduction by seed and subdivided into the Gymnosperms and Angiosperms.
Angiosperms: Acacia, sugarcane, Pisum, Triticum

Gymnosperms: Pinus, Cycas, Gingko
Fungi: Rhizopus
Related Theory
Gymnosperm and Angiosperm have a sporic life-cycle with sporophyte predominance, and seeds. The gametophyte is reduced to cells inside the ovule or pollen grain. Males have a minimum number of cells being three and females being four. The antheridia are absent and the archegonia are also reduced. Higher groups of seed plants lost flagellate spermatozoa and developed pollen tubes. The classes of Spermatophyta are Ginkgoopsida, Cycadopsida, Pinopsida, Gnetopsida, and Angiospermae.

Students confuse the option as option (A) and (B) also represents spermatophytes. But the question asked toclassify the Spermatophyta, which is divided into Gymnosperm and Angiosperm and option (D) represents both the divisions respectively.
